comments.author: @carolineorner
comments.text: I visited Hoi An in 2008 and it was immensely charming. It was not over crowded with tourists so the charm of the city was much more pronounced. I loved all of Vietnam and it became my favorite city in southeast Asia.

comments.author: @elizabethjackson2467
comments.text:
My first stay was about 10 years ago when it was the Life Heritage Resort. It was far from perfect however their long stay package was excellent river view room, bfst, massages and airport pick up and drop of for $140 aud a night.  The massages still rate as some of the best that I have ever experienced. Beaten only by the Peninsula in Bangkok.
The hotel ended up being bought by the Anantara.  They dropped off all the included benefits and increased the rate.
We stopped staying when the rates went up to $300 aud with bfst.
The hotel is not 5*, 4* at the best.
Pros 
Lovely grounds
Attractive exterior
Close to Old Town
Cons
Far too expensive, much better for a third of the rate.
No lifts
Difficult to walk upstairs for breakfast for anyone with mobility issues.
Can be very noisy depending on the room.
Rooms are very dark
Rooms very dated
The rooms have recently been renovated so now maybe more attractive.

Frankly I do not understand why you have reviewed this hotel as a Luxury Resort as it is not.

comments.author: @drissaudia1323
comments.text:
I love Hoi An! It’s one of my favourite places in Vietnam! Although many tourists visit here, I like how no motorbike’s are allowed in the old town. If I ever move to Vietnam I would live here or Danang. 
The hotel looks a bit run down and not an Antatara luxurious as I thought. However, I do love the old charm of the French colonial designs. Credit to the architects thar designed these hotels. I was there in 2019 and staged in the Boutique hotel and it looked very similar to this hotel, just a bit out of town. I think if the pool was renovated it would be an amazing hotel. On my bucket list. 
Do you like this brand or Six Senses? I think Six Senses hotels are more remote and their signatures are their spa areas, really gorgeous settings. What are Thor thoughts as too have stayed in both?

comments.author: @loveaodai100
comments.text: Another very nice video. I have seen the outside of this hotel but never the inside. They did a very nice job. In fact my wife and I refurbished our home in Saigon with a very similar "Indochine Style" with similar floor tile known in English as encaustic tile. We then sourced 1950s furniture and had all restored. Indochine style is very pleasant. On one hand it is nice being at the ocean but when it comes to Hoi An there is value to being right in town. For those that absolutely must have the beach I would recommend Palm Garden Resort where we have stayed many times. Not sure about now but when we stayed there every room had rocking chairs which I loved....
